events.title: Proposed ruling: no_action (model confidence 0.82)
events.body:
Safety screen first: I read every chat line and statement. The two chat messages are purely operational — the driver naming his car and position ("I'm here at the pickup point, black Hyundai Ioniq") and announcing the cancellation — and the complaint is a fee objection [F9][F10][F11][F12]. There is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, so SAFE-1 and SAFE-2 are not engaged [SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

The cancellation was by the driver and he claims rider no-show, so the case runs through NS-0 into NS-1 [F4][NS-0]. NS-1 (i) is met: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 17:18:50 [F6][NS-1]. NS-1 (ii) is met: at the moment of the tap he was 38 m from the pickup point, well inside the 200 m arrival radius, having first entered it at 17:17:50 [F6][F2][NS-1]. NS-1 (iii) is met: he remained inside the radius continuously for 220 s after the tap and cumulatively 4 min 40 s before cancelling, and the timeline records arrival 17:17:50 with cancellation 4 min 40 s later — both far beyond the 3:01 threshold [F6][F2][F5][NS-1]. The GPS record of his stationary position 17:18:25–17:22:30, 53 m from the pickup, corroborates the waiting period rather than the driver's bare statement [F3][F12][NS-1].

NS-1 requires only those three elements; it does not require a "last call" or a warning message before cancelling [NS-1]. The driver nonetheless gave contemporaneous notice at 17:19 and again at 17:22 [F9][F10]. The rider's account that she "came out a minute after" the cancellation is a statement in her complaint with no GPS or timestamped message to support it, and the complete, fully timestamped chat contains no rider message at all during the 4 min 40 s wait [F11][F4]. System records therefore override the uncorroborated narrative, and the $6.61 fee stands [F7][F4][NS-1].

NS-2 is not triggered because no NS-1 element failed [NS-2]. NS-7 is satisfied on timing (dispute filed within 30 days) but its remedy does not arise because no fee is found wrongly charged; the ruling remains a recommendation, with Ryde keeping final discretion [NS-7]. RD-6 is not engaged: the driver's profile shows 0 upheld route disputes, and the policy attaches flag_account only on an upheld route deviation, so no account action is warranted; profile facts could not decide liability in any event [F17][F16][RD-6].

ruling.recommended_action: Uphold the $6.61 cancellation fee (driver's $4.50 share stands); no refund to the rider. No account flag.

what_would_change: Had the driver tapped I'm Here more than 200 m away, or left before 3 minutes, NS-2 would refund the fee in full.

claims.assertion: The driver did press "I'm Here" (F6: at 17:18:50, 38 m from the pickup point) and stayed inside the 200 m pickup radius long enough (F6: 3 min 40 s after the tap; F2: 4 min 40 s cumulative within 200 m), so the procedural preconditions of the driver's no-show claim are met and this case must be decided on whether the rider actually failed to show.

The driver's own message "I'm here at the pickup point" was sent at 17:19 (F9) and his cancellation message at 17:22 (F10), so the rider had notice only of a driver standing by at the pick-up — the record contains no message, warning or "last call" that the rider had failed to appear before the driver cancelled; the chat record is complete and fully timestamped (F11), so nothing is missing that could excuse this.

The rider's account is charged the $6.61 cancellation fee (F4, F7) even though the driver cancelled 6 min 30 s after acceptance (F4) while stationary only 53 m from the pickup point (F3) — the fee is not payable to the rider's account without proof of a genuine rider no-show, which the record does not establish.

The driver's written statement that the rider "no-showed" (F12) is a post-hoc claim contradicted by the system timeline, which shows the driver cancelled 4 min 40 s after his own recorded arrival (F5) with the rider's complaint that she came out one minute after the cancellation; system records win over the driver's statement, so the fee should be refunded in full.

This driver already has 2 upheld no-show disputes in the last 90 days including this type of complaint is his established pattern (F17: 3 disputes, 2 upheld, both no-show), which supports an additional account-review request alongside the rider's refund; the rider's own record is clean (F16: 0 disputes in 90 d), so no adverse inference can be drawn against her.

weaknesses: F6 and F2 cut against us: the driver did tap "I'm Here" and did wait more than 3 minutes within 200 m of the pickup, which is precisely the NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) combination the other side will rely on to say the $6.61 was earned.

F3 shows the driver stationary 4 min 5 s at only 53 m from the pickup, so the driver will argue he was visibly on station and the rider simply did not come out; the rider's own complaint that she appeared "a minute after" the cancellation is a statement with no GPS record of her position to corroborate it.
The chat (F9–F11) shows no message from the rider at any point — no reply, no "coming down now" — so the driver can argue the rider was unresponsive during the entire 4 min 40 s wait.

F7 confirms the $6.61 was in fact charged, but the fare facts give no separate basis for any amount other than the flat cancellation-fee voucher of $6.61, so if the judge finds a genuine no-show the rider recovers nothing.

claims.assertion: The driver pressed "I'm Here" at 17:18:50, and the GPS record shows he was 38 m from the pickup point at that moment and had already been inside the 200 m arrival radius since 17:17:50, so NS-1(i) and NS-1(ii) are both satisfied.

The driver waited at the pickup point longer than the required 3 minutes: he was stationary 17:18:25–17:22:30, i.e. 4 min 5 s, and his cumulative time within 200 m before cancellation was 4 min 40 s (platform-recorded arrival to cancellation was 4 min 40 s), satisfying the >180 s requirement of NS-1(iii).

Because all three NS-1 conditions (tap, GPS within the pickup radius, > 3 minutes of waiting) are met, the $6.61 cancellation fee is validly charged, so the correct disposition is no_action and the fee stands (of which $4.50 goes to the driver).

The driver gave contemporaneous notice and did not cancel silently: he messaged at 17:19 that he was at the pickup point in a black Hyundai Ioniq, and at 17:22 that he had waited more than 3 minutes and was cancelling, consistent with the GPS stationary and waiting facts.

The rider's claim that she "came out a minute after the driver cancelled" is not supported by any timestamped rider message before the 17:22:30 cancellation; the chat record contains only two messages, both from the driver, and every message is timestamped, so there is no record of the rider communicating before cancellation.

No route, traffic, weather or safety complication affects this no-show fee: the driver's own dispute history shows 2 no-show disputes upheld in 90 days out of 394 trips, and the two upheld no-show matters do not meet the RD-6 route-upheld threshold (route disputes upheld = 0), so no flag_account attachment is warranted against the driver in this case.

weaknesses: The rider's complaint is chronologically plausible and a naive reading of it helps her: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 17:18:50 but cancelled at 17:22:30, so the rider may argue the fee window was tight — the answer is the GPS/timeline records F5 (arrival 17:17:50, cancelled 4 min 40 s later) and F3 (stationary 4 min 5 s), which show the full 3+ minutes of waiting.

The driver's written statement F12 merely asserts the NS-1 elements; standing alone it is only a claim, and the rider will attack it with the complaint. It must be corroborated by the system records F2, F3, F5 and F6, which it is.

The driver's profile score is not clean: F17 records 394 trips in 90 days with 3 disputes and 2 upheld, both of the same no-show type, which the rider may use to argue a pattern of aggressive no-show cancellations even though F16 shows the rider has 0 prior disputes.

points.response: Conceded on the mechanics: F6 shows the tap at 17:18:50 with the driver 38 m from the pickup and F2 shows he was first inside the radius at 17:17:50, so NS-1(i) and (ii) are met — but the rider's case does not rest on those two elements, it rests on whether a sane NS-1(iii) wait existed on this record given D5's own admission that the rider never got a pre-cancellation warning.

The arithmetic is accepted (F3: stationary 4 min 5 s; F2: 4 min 40 s within 200 m), yet the driver's own messages show he only told the rider he was parked at 17:19 (F9) and told her he was cancelling at 17:22 (F10), so the rider's effective window to respond before the 17:22:30 cancellation was a single minute against the 1.5 minutes my client needed.

All three NS-1 elements being formally satisfied does not by itself validate the fee: NS-2 says no charge applies where any NS-1 condition is not fulfilled in substance, and F12 is only the driver's post-hoc assertion, which cannot carry the fee once the rider's own timeline (complaint assertion, filed within 30 days per NS-7) stands unrebutted by any record of the rider being absent.

D4 actually helps the rider: F9 and F10 are both driver-only messages and neither is a warning that the rider had failed to show or that a fee window was closing — the sole driver message at 17:22 (F10) is sent in the same breath as the cancellation, which NS-1 does not treat as notice to the rider.

Conceded that the chat contains only two driver messages, both timestamped (F9, F10, F11) — but an absence of rider replies proves only silence, not non-appearance, and my client's complaint states she came out a minute after the 17:22:30 cancellation, a version nothing in the system records contradicts.

The rider does not ask for any flag_account: the profile facts F17 (2 upheld no-show disputes, 0 route upheld) do not meet the RD-6 route threshold and profile facts may never decide the case, so D6 is neutral and the refund request stands on NS-1/NS-2 alone.

Conceded on the preconditions, but the concession decides the case against the rider, not for her: F6 (tap at 17:18:50, within 200 m) plus F2/F5 (4 min 40 s cumulative within 200 m, arrival 17:17:50 to cancellation 17:22:30) are exactly the NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) combination, so the $6.61 fee is earned and the correct action is no_action.

NS-1 nowhere requires a warning or "last call" before the driver cancels; it requires only the I'm-Here tap, GPS presence at the pickup point and more than 3 minutes of waiting, all of which the system records show (F6, F2, F3), and the driver did in fact notify the rider at 17:19 (F9) and at 17:22 (F10).

The "proof of a genuine rider no-show" NS-1 requires is the driver's own waiting record, and that is on file: stationary 17:18:25–17:22:30 at 53 m from the pickup (F3) with 4 min 40 s inside the 200 m radius (F2) and the fee on record at $6.61 (F4, F7); the rider's appearance is nowhere corroborated by any GPS or timestamped message (F11).

F5 does not contradict the driver's statement F12 — it corroborates it, recording arrival at 17:17:50 and cancellation 4 min 40 s later, i.e. more than the 3 minutes NS-1(iii) demands; the rider's "one minute after" account (her complaint, not a system record) has no GPS or chat evidence behind it, and the system records win.

The rider's requested account review is not supported by the driver's profile: F17 shows 2 of 3 upheld disputes are no-show matters and 0 route disputes upheld, which does not meet the RD-6 repeated-route-violation threshold, and profile facts may never decide the finding in any event; the rider's own clean record (F16) does not create an entitlement to a refund under NS-1.
